title: Storm Clouds Are Rising
next_chapter_hook: Just as Chen Ji was about to set his strategic pieces, a remnant soul emerged from the Tianji Record—Mo Xiansheng brought mysterious news about the Imperial Dynasty, and the entire chess game was about to be reshuffled.

text.content: Within the secret chamber, seven eerie blue soul lamps hung in mid-air, arranged according to the Big Dipper constellation. Chen Ji stood at the formation's core, surrounding runes writhing like living creatures, carving a massive cage beneath his feet. 'The first deadly trap... is nothing more than this.' He murmured to himself, gazing over those supposedly exquisite mechanisms, a hint of disdain flickering in his eyes. The flow of runes, the flickering of soul lamps, the barely perceptible spiritual energy fluctuations in the air—all appeared before his eyes like an unfolded chess manual, transparently ridiculous.

He raised his hand and slowly retrieved a yellowed talisman paper from his chest. This was an imitation of the Tianji Record Fragment, lacking prophetic abilities but capable of disrupting the formation's perception. As the talisman paper touched the ground, it silently ignited, transforming into a wisp of blue smoke. The next moment, all seven soul lamps extinguished simultaneously, plunging the entire secret chamber into absolute silence. Yet beneath Chen Ji's feet, the cage runes had quietly fractured three of their main veins.

dialogue.content: 'Next time, put more effort into it, Eye of Heavenly Dao.' Chen Ji straightened his robe, stepping over the deactivated formation mechanisms, heading deeper into the secret chamber. 'Your chess moves... are far too crude.' His voice echoed in the darkness, carrying an offhand mockery. This was his first confrontation with the unseen chess player, and he had already claimed the initial victory.

text.content: At the chamber's end stood a stone door, bearing an antiquated sect emblem—a Tianqing Sect symbol abandoned a century ago. Chen Ji's fingers traced the worn engravings, his heart stirring slightly. The existence of this secret chamber was likely unknown even to the current sect leader, Ling Yuan. It belonged to an intentionally erased history, a secret about which even the Tianji Record had left only fragmentary hints.

choice.prompt: A secret seems hidden beyond the stone door, and Chen Ji must decide—whether to explore immediately, or first return to Tianqing Sect to prepare for rescuing his sister Chen Nian?

choices.text: Push open the door and investigate the secret
choices.description: Since we've come this far, there's no reason to leave empty-handed. The secret behind the stone door might be related to Chen Nian's whereabouts—it's worth the risk.
choices.visible_reward: Might obtain crucial clues or treasures
choices.risk_hint: Unknown dangers may lie beyond the door

text.content: The stone door was heavy and ancient, its surface thick with moss and weathered marks of time. Chen Ji channeled his spiritual energy, pressing both palms against the door and pushing with force. A sharp crack echoed as the long-sealed mechanism stirred to life, the stone door slowly creaking open. A musty stench rushed toward him, mixed with an indescribable fragrance—the unique aroma of ancient spiritual herbs.

choices.text: Temporarily seal and return to the sect
choices.description: The countdown to July seventh won't wait, and Chen Nian's safety is more urgent. This secret can be explored another day.
choices.visible_reward: Ensure ample time for the rescue plan
choices.risk_hint: The stone door secret might be discovered by others

text.content: Chen Ji withdrew his hands and stepped back. This place was too eerie—he had no desire to venture deeper without preparation. He retrieved a special sealing talisman from his chest and pressed it onto the stone door. It was an ancient talisman he'd obtained through a serendipitous encounter, capable of blocking spiritual detection. Once he'd dealt with Chen Nian's situation, returning to uncover this secret wouldn't be too late.

After leaving the secret chamber, Chen Ji didn't head directly back to his quarters. Instead, he detoured to the outer sect's scripture library. There, among countless texts accumulated over centuries by Tianqing Sect, lay a volume titled 'Major Events of Tianqing,' documenting important historical events of the sect. Clues about the forgotten upheaval a century ago might be found within its pages.

The library's caretaker was a deaf, visually impaired elder, dozing peacefully in a chair. Chen Ji moved silently through towering bookshelves, ultimately discovering the dusty tome tucked away in the most secluded corner. As he rapidly flipped through yellowed pages, his eyes scanning each one, his fingers abruptly halted—a page's edge had been torn away, leaving jagged marks.

dialogue.content: 'Interesting.' Chen Ji murmured softly, bringing the damaged page closer. The missing content spanned approximately three lines, with remaining ink hints suggesting connections to the 'Imperial Dynasty' and 'Heavenly Secrets.' Who had torn away this content, and when? Why tear it? His mind rapidly sketched a vague outline—within Tianqing Sect's history, there had existed a deliberately erased period, potentially connected to the Tianji Record's transmission.

text.content: Just as he prepared to investigate further, footsteps echoed outside the scripture library. Chen Ji swiftly closed the ancient tome, tucked it back in its original spot, then walked calmly toward the entrance. An inner sect disciple entered, surprise flickering across their face upon seeing Chen Ji, which quickly transformed into customary disdain. What was a废物杂役 doing in the scripture library? Chen Ji lowered his head respectfully, stepping aside—but the corners of his mouth lifted slightly.

dialogue.content: 'Chen废物, what brings you here?' The inner sect disciple deliberately raised his voice. 'Don't tell me you came to steal cultivation manuals? With your废物资质, reading them would be pointless.' His companions burst into mocking laughter. Chen Ji offered no retort, silently lowering his head like a startled quail—but anyone observing closely would notice the fleeting cold gleam in his eyes. 废物? After July seventh, let's see who the real废物 is.

choice.prompt: Faced with the inner sect disciple's mockery, Chen Ji must decide how to respond—whether to endure it completely and maintain his persona, or give a small demonstration to embarrass his mocker?

choices.text: Continue to endure and build up the persona
choices.description: The core of playing dumb to devour the tiger lies in playing the 'pig' convincingly enough. It's still not time to reveal anything. Let these people keep laughing.
choices.visible_reward: Maintain the persona without arousing suspicion
choices.risk_hint: May affect the opinions of others present

dialogue.content: "You seniors are right, I just came to see if there are any crude cultivation techniques that a servant can learn." Chen Ji's voice was low and humble, as if he truly felt ashamed of his waste-level spiritual roots. He walked past the group of Inner Disciples with his head bowed, his figure desolate and pitiful. Only after he had walked far from the scripture archive did he slowly straighten his waist, the coldness in his eyes gradually receding, and a faint smile tugging at the corner of his lips.

text.content: The group of Inner Disciples continued laughing loudly behind him, completely unaware that the object of their mockery had already memorized each and every one of their contemptible faces. Chen Ji walked extremely slowly, slow enough to hear every voice and remember every sneering countenance. These people... would all be useful someday. It was perfectly natural for a废物 (waste) servant to be bullied, but what expressions would those who had bullied him wear if the废物 suddenly rose to power? Just thinking about it brought him joy.

choices.text: A subtle counterattack in the shadows
choices.description: Don't reveal strength, but can use words to make the opponent embarrassed. A废物 can also have backbone, just needs to have it skillfully.
choices.visible_reward: Restore some dignity in front of onlookers
choices.risk_hint: Acting too wise will attract attention

dialogue.content: Chen Ji stopped and slowly turned around. His expression remained humble, but his gaze was unexpectedly calm. "You seniors are right, I am indeed a废物." He paused, then added, "But I heard that the founding ancestor of Tianqing Sect also started as a servant. Since you seniors are paying such close attention to me, I suppose you think I have the makings of an ancestor?" His voice was not loud, yet it silenced the entire scripture archive. Those Inner Disciples stared at each other, at a loss for words—for a moment—did this废物 just lose his mind? How dare he use the ancestor to pressure them?

text.content: "You!" The leading Inner Disciple's face flushed red, and he stepped forward wanting to strike, but was pulled back by his companion. Private fighting was forbidden inside the scripture archive—this was sect law. And Chen Ji had already lowered his head again, resuming his timid appearance, as if the earlier words had merely been their imagination. But the surrounding disciples who had come to watch exchanged meaningful glances—this Chen Ji seemed rather different from the rumors.

After returning to his dilapidated little room, Chen Ji took out a yellowed map from under his pillow. This was intelligence he had spent three years collecting from various sources about where Chen Nian might be imprisoned. The Holy Sect's sphere of influence, the border areas of the three major sects, and the forbidden lands that even maps refused to mark—he had marked them all. And now, among those密密麻麻 (dense) markings, he added another point: the Imperial Dynasty.

dialogue.content: "Imperial Dynasty..." Chen Ji murmured to himself, his finger lingering on those two characters for a long time. In a cultivator's understanding, the Imperial Dynasty was an ethereal existence—superior to the sects, yet never proactively interfering in cultivator affairs. Legends about it were scarce, with only occasional fragments mentioned in ancient texts. But one thing was certain: an existence that even the three major sects dared not provoke was no ordinary power.

text.content: Chen Ji closed his eyes, his consciousness sinking deep into the Mental Sea. There floated a broken page—the first page of the Tianji Record. The ink was blurred, with ancient characters and diagrams faintly visible. Three years now, this fragment had accompanied him through countless life-and-death moments, yet it also gradually devoured his Heavenly Fate. Every glimpse of the future came at a price. And his Heavenly Fate Value was nearly exhausted.

Just then, that fragment suddenly emitted a faint glow. Chen Ji's heart stirred—this was the sign that Mo Xiansheng was about to appear. That mysterious soul fragment guardian was his nominal 'master,' as well as the key figure in the Tianji Record's inheritance. Normally he rarely appeared on his own, only manifesting when Chen Ji faced major decisions or obtained key clues. And now he had come—this meant what was about to happen was far more important than Chen Ji had imagined.

dialogue.content: "You found that secret chamber." The old and ethereal voice rang in Chen Ji's mind, carrying a hint of praise. "Faster than I anticipated." Above the fragment, a faint phantom slowly formed. It was an elderly man with white hair, his features too blurred to distinguish, but those eyes were exceptionally bright, as if they could pierce through all illusions.

"Mo Xiansheng." Chen Ji responded in his heart. "What's in that secret chamber? Is it related to the Tianji Record's inheritance?" The phantom was silent for a moment, then slowly shook his head. "Those are things your father left behind, but they are not something you can touch yet." He paused, then added, "However, since you've come this far, there are some things you should know."

choice.prompt: Mo Xiansheng seemed prepared to reveal important information, and Chen Ji needed to decide what attitude to take—humble inquiry, or proactive questioning?

choices.text: Humbly seek guidance and wait for revelation
choices.description: Mo Xiansheng knew far more than him, and rushing would only backfire. Remain respectful and let this mysterious master unveil the mystery initiative
choices.visible_cost: Need to be patient and wait
choices.risk_hint: The other party may have only said part of it.

dialogue.content: Chen Ji did not press further, merely nodding slightly as if accepting instruction. Mo Xiansheng's phantom seemed satisfied and nodded, then spoke: 'Do you know why the three great sects have stood in equilibrium until now, yet none has ever unified the cultivation world?' Chen Ji considered for a moment and replied: 'Because they check and balance each other? No one can swallow the others.'

text.content: 'That is merely the surface,' Mo Xiansheng's voice turned low and grave. 'The true reason is—the Empire does not permit it.' These words struck Chen Ji's heart like a heavy hammer. Mo Xiansheng continued: 'Do you think the cultivation world is a lawless wilderness where the strong prey on the weak? You are mistaken. In this land, an invisible hand controls everything. The three great sects, the Holy Sect, and even all the forbidden lands and secret realms... are all under the Empire's watchful gaze.'

dialogue.content: 'And now, the Empire is about to make its move.' Mo Xiansheng's phantom began to fade. 'July seventh... is not merely a date, but a signal. The 'Heavenly Fate Lock Key' on your sister Chen Nian's body is exactly what the Empire needs. That is why the Holy Sect attacked her at this moment—because they sensed the Empire's imminent intervention.' Chen Ji's pupils constricted sharply. The truth behind Chen Nian's capture was far more complex than he had imagined!

'What can I do?' Chen Ji急切地问道 in his heart. Mo Xiansheng's phantom had faded to near invisibility, but his aged voice still echoed: 'Remember, before the Empire, the three great sects are all chess pieces. And you...' The voice abruptly stopped, the last few words seemingly forcibly erased by some power. But Chen Ji had understood—he must find his own position in this grander game of chess.

text.content: Mo Xiansheng's phantom had completely dissipated, the fragment returning to its original dim state. But Chen Ji remained motionless for a long time, his mind continuously replaying the conversation. The Empire... Heavenly Secrets' Eye... Heavenly Fate Lock Key... These seemingly unrelated clues were gradually weaving into a massive web in his mind. And he had unknowingly become a crucial piece within that web.

Outside the window, the setting sun sank, dyeing Tianqing Sect in golden crimson. Distant mountain peaks loomed hazily in the twilight, like hidden beasts. Chen Ji rose and walked to the window, gazing at the land where he had lived for three years. The faction of one of the three great sects' sect master, the mysterious Holy Sect, the hidden imperial forces... all chess players had taken their positions. And he, a former waste servant, was about to spark his own storm in this game involving the entire cultivation world.

'Chen Nian...' Chen Ji murmured his sister's name, the coldness in his eyes gradually sharpening into a blade. 'Wait for me.' He turned to the desk, took out brush and ink, and began writing a dense plan on blank paper. July seventh—still twenty-one days away. In these twenty-one days, he must prepare thoroughly—because when that day arrives, he would face not just those useless pursuers from the Holy Sect, but a leviathan that even the three great sects must reckon with.

Night descended gradually, and the lights of Tianqing Sect flickered on one by one. Only a dim oil lamp illuminated Chen Ji's room, reflecting his figure hunched over the desk writing urgently. On that paper, he had drawn the entire layout of Tianqing Sect, marking the position and movements of every key figure. At the edge of the map, he had heavily circled three names in cinnabar—Ling Yuan, Han Lie, and a title he had never encountered before: Imperial Emissary. The chess game had been laid out, and every piece he was about to place would determine victory or defeat.

When the final brushstroke fell, Chen Ji finally exhaled deeply. He carefully folded the paper filled with plans and tucked it into his chest. Then he extinguished the oil lamp and sat quietly in the darkness. The Tianji Record fragment warmed slightly in his mind—a warning that danger was approaching, though he still could not see what specifically. But it didn't matter. Starting tomorrow, he would officially begin his arrangements. Tianqing Sect, Xuanwu Sect, Vermillion Bird Sect... all people would become pieces on his chessboard.
And he, Chen Ji, would be the one holding the pieces.

Outside the window, the moon emerged from behind the clouds, casting a wisp of cold light into the room. Chen Ji raised his head, gazing at that bright moon, silver light reflecting in his eyes. He remembered three years ago—that night when he was still a freshly transmigrated unlucky fellow, facing this useless body and certain death, almost wanting to give up. But now, everything was different. He had the Tianji Record, Mo Xiansheng's guidance, and more importantly—he had a goal.

'Wait,' he said softly, as if making a promise to someone. 'When I crush all my enemies beneath my feet, when I find Chen Nian, when I unravel all the secrets of the Tianji Record... at that time, I will let the entire cultivation world know—' The corner of his mouth slightly lifted, forming a faint, serene smile. '—what a true waste truly means.' The words fell, and silence reclaimed the room. And in that silence, some hidden existence deep within Tianqing Sect seemed to stir slightly. The gears of destiny were accelerating.

The next morning, Tianqing Sect operated as usual. Outer disciples did their morning lessons, inner disciples cultivated and sparred, elders handled sect affairs. Everything appeared identical to any other day, but only Chen Ji knew—beneath this calm surface, undercurrents had already begun to surge. He went to the Servants' Quarters early, doing the most menial work as always. But his eyes inadvertently swept past every passing disciple, every suspicious corner. Ling Yuan's people had already begun acting... he must complete his arrangements before them.

At noon, Chen Ji entered the inner disciples' training grounds under the pretext of delivering tea. This was where Su Qingyao frequently appeared. As the Inner Disciple Senior Fellow, every move she made attracted attention. And what Chen Ji needed was precisely the intelligence about the Holy Sect's hideout in her possession. He carried the tea tray, walking humbly along the edge of the training grounds, appearing to be just an insignificant servant, while every nerve was capturing information from the surroundings. Su Qingyao was in the eastern pavilion, discussing something with a few junior disciples. Her gaze occasionally swept toward Chen Ji, a cryptic light flickering in her eyes.

'You, the servant, come here to refill the tea.' An inner disciple called out. Chen Ji hastily jogged over, skillfully adding hot water to the teapot. The moment he turned to leave, a hand suddenly landed on his shoulder. His heart tightened, but on the surface, he maintained a fearful expression as he slowly turned around—it was Su Qingyao.

dialogue.content: 'Chen Ji, correct?' Su Qingyao's voice was cold and distant, no different from usual. 'I remember you. Last time outside the scripture hall, you had a conflict with those inner disciples.' Chen Ji lowered his head, putting on a frightened appearance: 'Senior Sister Su, th-that was a misunderstanding, I...' Before he could finish, Su Qingyao interrupted: 'I'm not saying you were wrong.' Her gaze fixed intently on Chen Ji's eyes, as if trying to see through some flaw. 'I just feel that you... are not quite the same as the rumors suggest.'

Chen Ji's heart rate slightly accelerated, but his expression still maintained that timid facade. He knew Su Qingyao was the most perceptive person in the entire Tianqing Sect, and also the most likely to discover his secret. For three years, he had countless times passed by her, countless times escaped her investigations. But every time facing her scrutiny, he dared not be the slightest bit careless. 'Senior Sister Su jests,' he lowered his head, his voice barely a whisper. 'I just got lucky and managed to survive.'

Su Qingyao stared at him for a moment, then released his shoulder and stepped back. Her expression revealed neither joy nor anger, only saying indifferently: 'Be more careful recently. Something seems about to happen within the sect.' After a pause, she added, 'Some troubled waters are not something someone at your cultivation level should wade into.' With that, she turned and left, leaving Chen Ji standing in confusion. But only Chen Ji himself knew that beneath that 'confused' expression, his mind was racing—Was Su Qingyao warning him? Or testing him? Or perhaps... she had already sensed something?

text.content: In any case, Su Qingyao's warning indicated one thing: the undercurrents within Tianqing Sect were more turbulent than he had imagined. Ling Yuan's movements had already begun affecting ordinary disciples, and those who could perceive this clearly were clearly not just Su Qingyao. Chen Ji carried the empty tea tray and slowly exited the training grounds. His back view remained humble and desolate, but his steps were steadier than when he had arrived. The good show... had just begun.

After leaving the training grounds, Chen Ji did not return to the Servants' Quarters. Instead, he took a detour to a secluded corner of Tianqing Sect Back Mountain. There was an unremarkable large stone, his secret meeting point with Ye Qing over three years. He took out a black jade pendant from his chest and pressed it against the stone's surface. After a moment, the jade pendant grew warm, and a faint trace of demonic energy leaked out—that was Ye Qing's response. 'The intelligence about the Holy Sect's hideout has been obtained,' Chen Ji silently recited in his heart. 'And also... news about the Empire.' The chess game at Tianqing Sect had just begun, and the pieces he had placed were taking their positions one by one.

Storm clouds gathering, mountain rain about to pour. When Chen Ji stood beside that large stone, watching the setting sun gradually sink beyond the mountains, he knew—his era was truly about to arrive. The Empire, the three great sects, the Holy Sect... all forces would be reshuffled in the impending storm. And he, in the identity of a waste, would control this chess game involving the fate of the entire cultivation world. July seventh—still twenty days. The countdown... had already begun.

Night deepened, and Tianqing Sect's silhouette became blurred in the darkness. Chen Ji took one last look at the land where he had lived for three years, then turned and walked toward his small hut. Tonight, he needed a good rest—because from tomorrow onward, he would have not a moment's peace. He had to complete his arrangements before Ling Yuan discovered his true identity, find Chen Nian before the Empire intervened, and step by step approach that final truth under the gaze of Heavenly Secrets' Eye. And at this moment, high above where he could not see, some existence beyond human comprehension was quietly observing all this with those invisible eyes.

Heavenly Secrets' Eye... and the Empire hidden behind everything. Chen Ji's true opponent was far more terrifying than he had imagined. But so what? Chen Ji had never feared the strong throughout his life. The stronger the enemy, the more intense the thrill of defeating them. With this thought, Chen Ji slowly closed his eyes. Tomorrow would be an entirely new day. And he was ready. The moment before he fell into slumber, the Tianji Record fragment warmed once more—Mo Xiansheng's voice rang in his mind, carrying a hint of urgency: 'Be careful, the Empire's people... are already on their way.'

Chen Ji's eyes snapped open, all drowsiness gone. He sat up and stared at the pitch-black night sky outside the window, a fierce light flickering in his eyes. The Empire's people... arriving faster than he had anticipated. What did this mean? Was it because of the 'Heavenly Fate Lock Key' on Chen Nian? Or had he triggered some forbidden mechanism? In any case, he had to speed up. The original twenty-day plan might now need to be

"Since it's like this..." Chen Ji murmured to himself, rising from the bed and walking to the desk where he lit an oil lamp. He took out the paper filled with plans and added a few more words next to "July Seventh": "Imperial Court intervention, time unknown." Looking at that line, he suddenly smiled—that kind of smile that becomes even more excited in desperation. "Interesting," he murmured, "it seems even Heaven thinks my past three years were too comfortable." He picked up his brush and began rapidly modifying the plan on the paper. Time wasn't enough? Then make the plan more aggressive. Risk was too high? Then take an even bigger risk.

He wrote filled three pages in one breath, not stopping until the eastern sky began to glow with the light before dawn. The window's sky had already turned slightly bright, a new day was about to arrive. Chen Ji stood up, stretching his stiff body, then took out the fragment of the Tianji Record from his chest. He gazed at that yellowish paper and murmured: "Master Mo, is there anything else you need to tell me?" The fragment warmed slightly, but no voice came. It seemed Master Mo had already said everything that needed to be said—what remained depended on his own fortune.

Chen Ji put away the fragment, changed into a clean servant's robe, and pushed open the door to walk out of the small hut. The Tianqing Sect in the early morning was shrouded in a light mist, appearing especially serene. The distant mountain peaks were half-hidden in the morning fog, like a splash-ink landscape painting. But Chen Ji knew this tranquility was merely superficial. Beneath those clouds and mist, countless pairs of eyes were watching from the shadows, countless hearts were beating nervously. And he was about to become the pebble that shattered this tranquility.

He took a deep breath and began laying out a new day's arrangements. First, he needed to see Ye Qing to obtain detailed intelligence about the Holy Sect's hideout. Then, he needed to find an opportunity to get close to Su Qingyao to see if he could obtain more internal information about the sect from her. Finally, he also needed to go to the outer sect's spiritual materials warehouse—where some alchemy materials he urgently needed were stored, and with his servant identity, obtaining those materials would require considerable effort. Everything was proceeding according to plan.

But just as he was passing through the inner sect plaza, a familiar figure appeared before him—it was Ling Yuan. That seemingly kind and amicable old sect master was standing in the center of the plaza, seemingly waiting for someone. When his gaze fell on Chen Ji, the corners of his mouth slightly lifted, revealing a meaningful smile. "Chen Ji," he spoke, his voice as gentle as if caring for a family junior, "rising so early?"

dialogue.content: Chen Ji's footsteps slightly faltered, but quickly returned to normal. He lowered his head and hurried forward, bowing respectfully: "Disciple greets the Sect Master Ancestor." Ling Yuan slightly nodded, his gaze lingering on Chen Ji for a moment, seemingly observing something. "How is your recent cultivation going?" he asked casually, his tone relaxed as if making small talk. But Chen Ji acutely sensed that within those turbid old eyes, a dangerous glint was flickering. This old fox... was probing him.

"Reporting to Sect Master Ancestor, this disciple's talent is dull, cultivation progress is slow," Chen Ji lowered his head, his voice respectful and humble, "I'm afraid this lifetime I won't even reach late-stage Qi Refining." Upon hearing this, Ling Yuan sighed: "What a pity, if you had good talent, you would certainly shine in our Tianqing Sect." He patted Chen Ji's shoulder—that hand seemed old and powerless, but when it landed on Chen Ji's shoulder, it carried a faint, intangible pressure. "Cultivate diligently, don't give up. Perhaps one day, opportunity will come."

Chen Ji lowered his head, repeatedly agreeing. But after Ling Yuan turned and left, his gaze instantly turned ice-cold. This old thing... had already begun to suspect him. Last night's appearance of Master Mo might have already been noticed by him. Speed must be accelerated. Otherwise, before the Imperial Court's people arrived, Ling Yuan would make the first move against him. With this thought, Chen Ji hurried toward the Rear Mountain. Ye Qing's intelligence, the sooner obtained the better.

text.content: Beside the huge rock at the Rear Mountain, a black figure was already waiting. Ye Qing still had that enchanting and seductive appearance, but the heaviness in her eyes revealed her inner tension. "You came earlier than I expected," she spoke, her voice much lower than usual, "I see you've also received the news." "What news?" Chen Ji frowned slightly, "I thought you would have intelligence here." Ye Qing's expression changed: "You didn't receive it? The Imperial Court... the Imperial Court's envoys left the imperial city three days ago and are heading this way."

dialogue.content: Chen Ji's pupils suddenly constricted. They set off three days ago? That meant they would arrive in at most half a month? Even faster than Master Mo had warned! This discovery made his heart sink. "The Imperial Court envoys... what cultivation level?" he asked. Ye Qing was silent for a moment, then uttered two words: "Hua Shen (Transcending Divinity)." Transcending Divinity stage! In the cultivation world's pyramid, this was already an existence standing at the apex. Most elders of the three great sects had Golden Core or Yuan Ying cultivation; those who could reach Transcending Divinity were all renowned figures. And the Imperial Court sent Transcending Divinity-stage envoys at the outset—the depth of their heritage was由此可见一斑.

result_nodes.description: Time is pressing; cannot be led by Master Mo's nose. He must take the initiative to strike, asking the most core questions.

dialogue.content: "Master Mo," Chen Ji spoke directly in his heart, without any preamble, "What is the relationship between the Imperial Court and the Eye of Heavenly Secrets? Why would Chen Nian become their target?" The illusory figure on the fragment slightly paused, seemingly not expecting Chen Ji to ask so directly. After a moment of silence, Master Mo sighed: "You are indeed clever... yes, the Imperial Court and the Eye of Heavenly Secrets do have a connection."

text.content: "Throughout the generations, every holder of the Tianji Record eventually faces two choices—becoming a piece on the Eye of Heavenly Secrets' chessboard, or being completely erased by it." Master Mo's voice became low, "And the Imperial Court... is the Eye of Heavenly Secrets' representative in the mortal world. Their purpose is to ensure every 'anomaly' is controlled within the correct path of destiny." Chen Ji's fists unconsciously tightened. So that's how it was... from the moment he obtained the Tianji Record, he had already become prey of the Eye of Heavenly Secrets.

dialogue.content: "What about my father then?" Chen Ji pressed on, "How did he die? Was it because he resisted the Eye of Heavenly Secrets?" Master Mo's illusory figure violently trembled, and after a long while spoke: "Your father... was the only person who almost broke this chess game. He could have become the most perfect piece for the Eye of Heavenly Secrets, but he chose another path." After a pause, he added, "And your sister Chen Nian is precisely the last move he left behind. The Heavenly Fate Lock... is the flaw in this chess game, and also your only hope."

As soon as the words fell, Master Mo's illusory figure began to dissipate. He seemed to have consumed a great deal of power from revealing too much information. Before vanishing, he left one final sentence: "Remember, before the Imperial Court... you are not fighting alone." Then, the fragment completely dimmed. Chen Ji sat alone in the darkness, digesting the information just obtained. The Imperial Court was the Eye of Heavenly Secrets' representative, Chen Nian was the Heavenly Fate Lock, and he himself... was an anomaly that should have been erased. But now, he had an opportunity to counterattack.

result_nodes.description: Some things don't need asking to know the answers. Master Mo's attitude itself revealed much information; he chose silence to see what the other party would proactively say.

text.content: Chen Ji did not speak, simply waiting quietly. The Master Mo on the fragment seemed surprised by his silence; the illusory figure slightly tilted its head, as if observing him. After a moment, Master Mo proactively spoke: "Don't you want to ask something?" Chen Ji slightly shook his head in his heart, still maintaining silence. He knew that for a being like Master Mo, what they feared most wasn't people who asked many questions, but those who made them unable to see through.

"As expected, when Chen Ji didn't answer, Mo Xiansheng took the initiative: 'The Dynasty... is a colossal force that stands above the sects. Its history is even longer than the combined history of the three major sects, with depths beyond measure.' His voice grew low, 'And now, the Dynasty has taken an interest in the Tianji Record. Before your father disappeared, he had an undisclosed contact with the Dynasty. The specifics of that contact, I don't know. But I know it was that experience that made your father decide to pass the Tianji Record to you, rather than acting according to the Dynasty's arrangements.'"

dialogue.content: "'As for your sister Chen Nian...' Mo Xiansheng paused, 'Her 'Heavenly Fate Lock-Key' constitution was deliberately arranged by your father. This constitution can interfere with the Tianji Record's foresight, creating cracks in destiny. The Dynasty wants her precisely to seal these cracks.' Hearing this, Chen Ji finally gained some understanding. So Chen Nian's existence was the final move his father had set in place. And now, he must complete this move—finding her before the Dynasty does, and awakening the power within her.'"

"'The help I can give you is limited,' Mo Xiansheng's phantom began to blur, 'but there is one thing I can tell you—within the Tianqing Sect, there is someone secretly colluding with the Dynasty. He hasn't yet discovered your true identity, but his informants are everywhere throughout the sect. Be careful.' After saying this, Mo Xiansheng's phantom dissipated completely. Chen Ji opened his eyes, gazing at the sky gradually darkening outside the window. The Dynasty, Ling Yuan, the Eye of Heavenly Dao... all the clues pointed to one fact: he had already stood at the center of the storm. And this storm would sweep through the entire cultivation world.'"

text.content: "Night fell, and the lights of the Tianqing Sect lit up one after another. Chen Ji sat in his small room, a blank sheet of paper spread before him. He didn't rush to write; instead, he closed his eyes, reviewing all the information he'd obtained that day in his mind. The Dynasty was the spokesperson of the Eye of Heavenly Dao, Chen Nian was the Heavenly Fate Lock-Key, there was a Dynasty informant within the Tianqing Sect, Ling Yuan had already begun to suspect him... each piece of information alone was merely fragments, but strung together, they outlined a clear picture.'"

"Chen Ji opened his eyes, lifted his pen, and wrote the first line on the paper: 'The chess game has changed; one must adapt to change.' The Dynasty's intervention, the three major sects vying for supremacy, the Demonic Path watching with hungry eyes—in such circumstances, sticking to the original plan would only lead to death. He had to disrupt all his enemies' expectations and find his own opportunity amidst the chaos. A Dynasty emissary at the Transformation God Stage... that was an existence capable of crushing everything. Direct confrontation would be no different from seeking death, but he had never been one for direct combat.'"

"He stopped his pen and fell into deep thought. Mo Xiansheng said there was a Dynasty informant within the Tianqing Sect—who could that be? Ling Yuan? Or someone else? If it was Ling Yuan, it made sense—he had been skipped over by the Tianji Record back then, and now colluding with the Dynasty, wanting to use the Dynasty's power for revenge and power grabs. As for Han Lie... that simple-minded genius from the Xuanwu Sect, he was probably just a pawn being used. With this thought, a cold smile curved Chen Ji's lips. This chess game was far more complex than he had imagined, but it was also full of opportunities. The more enemies, the greater the internal divisions. And what he excelled at most was finding breakthroughs within enemy divisions.'"

"Suddenly, footsteps came from outside the window. Chen Ji quickly put away the paper, lay back on the bed, and pretended to be in deep sleep. The door was gently pushed open, and a figure slipped in silently. Chen Ji narrowed his eyes, seeing the visitor's outline through the crack—Su Qingyao. This Inner Disciple Senior Fellow, coming to the quarters of a废物 servant like him in the middle of the night, what was she after?"

dialogue.content: "Su Qingyao stood by the bed for a moment, seemingly observing Chen Ji's sleeping appearance. After a long while, she spoke softly: 'I know you're not asleep.' Chen Ji opened his eyes but didn't get up, only turning his head to look at her: 'Senior Sister Su, visiting this late at night, may I ask what brings you here?' Su Qingyao didn't answer his question; instead, she directly said: 'The Sect Master Ancestor spoke with you today.' This wasn't a question but a statement. Chen Ji's heart tightened, though his expression remained calm: 'Senior Sister's information network is indeed efficient.'"

"'Chen Ji,' Su Qingyao's voice suddenly softened a bit, 'I don't know what secrets you're hiding, but I can feel... that you and I are the same kind of person.' Chen Ji was slightly stunned. Su Qingyao continued: 'Ling Yuan is not a good person, and his attention toward you won't be well-intentioned either. If you need help... you can come to me.' With that, she turned toward the door, leaving only a sentence: 'In three days, at the Inner Sect Martial Arena, I'll have a sparring match with Han Lie. If you're interested, you can come watch.' The door gently closed, footsteps gradually fading. Chen Ji lay on the bed, staring at the dim ceiling, not moving for a long time. Su Qingyao... how much did she know? And why was she helping him?"

text.content: "This night, Chen Ji barely slept at all. Su Qingyao's appearance had disrupted some of his plans, but it also brought new possibilities. If he could win her help, the接下来的行动会顺利很多。但同时，他也必须警惕——苏青瑶是整个天青宗最聪明的人，任何欺骗她的尝试都可能适得其反。思来想去，他最终决定暂且观望。三天后的演武场，或许是一个观察她真实态度的好机会。

"The next morning, Chen Ji went to report at the Servants' Quarters as usual. Today's task was to clean the Inner Sect's Scripture Library—a place he happened to need. While cleaning, he could take the opportunity to search for more information about the Dynasty and Tianqing Sect's history, killing two birds with one stone. The Scripture Library was still deserted; that deaf and blurry-eyed old man was still dozing. Chen Ji walked lightly past the rows of bookshelves, his gaze quickly scanning the spines. Suddenly, his eyes stopped on an inconspicuous old book in the corner—'Tianqing Secret Records'.'"

"Chen Ji calmly took down the book and opened the first page. On the yellowed paper was recorded a piece of forgotten history: 'When Tianqing was first established, it received appointment from the Dynasty, tasked with guarding the Eastern Sea Forbidden Grounds. All successive Sect Masters had to travel to the Dynasty capital for reports, until a hundred years ago...' The following content had been torn out, exactly the same as what he'd seen in 'Tianqing Major Events Chronicle'. What happened a hundred years ago? Why had the relationship between Tianqing Sect and the Dynasty been deliberately erased? These questions swirled endlessly in his mind.'"

"'Boy, what are you looking at?' An aged voice suddenly sounded behind him. Chen Ji turned to see the old administrator of the Scripture Library. The old man's turbid eyes fixed on the book in his hand, and his gaze suddenly became sharp, forming a stark contrast with his aged appearance. Chen Ji's heart stirred, but on the surface, he acted as if nothing had happened: 'Reporting to Elder, this disciple merely flipped through this book accidentally while cleaning, and didn't read it carefully.'"

dialogue.content: "The old man stared at him for a moment, then suddenly smiled: 'Interesting... how many years has it been since anyone dared to linger before this book for more than three breaths.' He approached Chen Ji, lowering his voice: 'If you want to know more, in three days, come find me at Moon-Gazing Pavilion on the Rear Mountain.' With that, he turned back to his seat and resumed his doze, as if the previous conversation had never happened. Chen Ji watched the old man's retreating figure, a thoughtful glint flickering in his eyes. This seemingly ordinary old man was probably also a highly skilled expert hiding his true abilities. The waters of Tianqing Sect... were deeper than he had imagined.'"

text.content: "After leaving the Scripture Library, Chen Ji returned to his small room. He organized all the information he'd obtained that day: Su Qingyao's show of goodwill, the mysterious old man's invitation, the Martial Arena in three days, and the Dynasty emissary who had yet to appear... all the clues pointed to the same fact—undercurrents churned within Tianqing Sect, and he stood precisely at the center of the whirlpool. The next three days would be a crucial period for positioning. Within these three days, he must acquire as much intelligence as possible, win over allies, and weaken enemies. The Martial Arena in three days might be his first stage to make his mark.'"

"Chen Ji took a deep breath and began formulating a detailed plan. First, the Martial Arena in three days, he must attend. This was not only an opportunity to observe Su Qingyao but also an excellent chance to get close to Han Lie and understand the Xuanwu Sect's movements. Second, the invitation from the Scripture Library old man was also worth accepting—if he could obtain intelligence about the relationship between Tianqing Sect and the Dynasty from him, it would greatly help his subsequent arrangements. Finally, he needed to maintain contact with Ye Qing, ensuring that intelligence from the Holy Sect's hideout could be obtained in time. Only by pursuing all three avenues could he gain the upper hand in the coming storm.'"

choice.prompt: "With limited time of three days, Chen Ji needed to decide which matter to prioritize—should he first meet the Scripture Library old man to obtain intelligence, or first improve the rescue plan through Ye Qing?"

choices.text: "Prioritize meeting the Scripture Library old man"
choices.description: "The relationship between the Dynasty and Tianqing Sect is the core secret. Since this old man dares to take the initiative to invite him, he must have something to rely on. Only by unraveling this mystery can other matters be resolved.'"
choices.risk_hint: "The old man's true intentions are unclear"

dialogue.content: "As night fell, Chen Ji quietly left his small room and headed toward Moon-Gazing Pavilion on the Rear Mountain. The moonlight was like water, illuminating the mountain path with dancing shadows. He walked extremely fast but slowed his pace as he approached the pavilion, vigilantly observing his surroundings. In Moon-Gazing Pavilion, a hunched figure stood with his back to him, quietly gazing at the bright moon in the night sky. 'You've come.' The old man's voice was calm and ancient, 'I thought you wouldn't dare come.'"

"Chen Ji entered the pavilion and bowed respectfully: 'With Elder summoning, how would this disciple dare not come?' The old man turned around; his turbid eyes appeared especially bright under the moonlight: 'Do you know why I called you here?' Chen Ji shook his head. The old man smiled, the smile carrying a hint of bitterness: 'Because you remind me of someone—a person from a hundred years ago who also liked to flip through old books in the Scripture Library.' Chen Ji's heart stirred: 'Elder means...'"

text.content: "'Your father, Chen Xuan.' When the old man spoke this name, there was a trace of nostalgia in his tone, 'He was the smartest person I ever met, and also the most tragic.' Chen Ji's breath slightly hitched. Chen Xuan—the father he had never met, the one who passed the Tianji Record to him. The old man continued: 'A hundred years ago, I witnessed him with my own eyes go from genius to outcast, and then from outcast to the pinnacle step by step. His Tianji Record... was the most complete volume I've ever seen.'"

dialogue.content: "The 'Complete Tianji Record'?" Chen Ji couldn't help but press further. "Didn't they say the Tianji Record has always been fragmented?" The old man shook his head. "That's merely what we tell outsiders. A hundred years ago, your father managed to repair the Tianji Record to an unprecedented level of completeness—seven full pages. But it was that very repair that led him to touch upon a forbidden secret." The old man's voice dropped. "The Imperial Court's forbidden secret."

"What exactly happened a hundred years ago?" Chen Ji pressed. The old man fell silent for a long moment before finally speaking: "That year, the Imperial Court sent envoys to the Tianqing Sect to take something away. Your father fought to the death to stop them, but he was hopelessly outnumbered. In the end, he used the power of the Tianji Record to seal that thing away, dividing the key into two parts—one in the Imperial Court's hands, and the other..." The old man paused. "On your sister, Chen Nian." Chen Ji's pupils constricted sharply. So that's it... Chen Nian becoming the Heavenly Fate Lock Key was no accident—it was inevitable.

text.content: "So that's why the Imperial Court is so eager to capture Chen Nian," Chen Ji murmured. "They want to obtain the complete key." The old man nodded: "You're very clever, even more composed than your father was in his youth. This is your greatest advantage, and also your greatest danger." He drew a yellowed journal from his chest and handed it to Chen Ji: "This is the information I've compiled over the years regarding the Imperial Court. Take it—perhaps it will be of help to you."
